balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Unilever PLC: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Unilever PLC: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Unilever PLC: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Unilever PLC: FY2025 statutory diluted EPS of EUR 4.32 is inflated by the one-off TMICC demerger gain. Diluted EPS on a continuing basis was EUR 2.59 (FY2024: EUR 2.44), on the post 8-for-9 consolidation share count -- that is the figure comparable across years, not the statutory one shown in this chart. The payout ratio (DPS / EPS) is also more meaningful measured against continuing EPS.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt
  • Statutory EPS spikes from disposal gains that will not recur

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Unilever PLC: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Unilever PLC: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Unilever PLC: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

capexSplit.title: CapEx split: PP&E vs intangibles
capexSplit.content:
Total CapEx is cash spent on fixed and intangible assets combined. This chart separates out purchase of intangibles (software, brands, IP); the remainder is spend on property, plant & equipment (PP&E) -- factories, machinery and distribution infrastructure.

For Unilever PLC: FY2025 CapEx of EUR 1,591m splits into EUR 1,417m PP&E and EUR 174m intangibles, down from EUR 1,971m total in FY2024 (EUR 1,738m PP&E / EUR 233m intangibles) as the Ice Cream demerger shrank the continuing asset base mid-year.

What to watch:

  • PP&E spend tracking manufacturing footprint changes (e.g. post-demerger site transfers)
  • Intangibles spend as a share of total, since it is far smaller and more discretionary than PP&E

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Unilever PLC: FY2025 statutory net income (EUR 9,469m) includes a EUR 3,373m one-off gain on the December 2025 demerger of the Ice Cream business (The Magnum Ice Cream Company, TMICC), booked in discontinued operations. Net income (continuing) at EUR 5,682m strips that gain out and is the comparable run-rate figure against FY2024's EUR 5,430m -- use it, not the statutory line, to judge underlying profitability.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • FY2025 is not comparable to prior years on a whole-company basis -- it excludes Ice Cream throughout

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Unilever PLC: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Unilever PLC: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
